answer: Each agent commits 16 GB of RAM and answers latency probes on pseudo-random offsets, so the cipher proof is bound to one physical machine: the verifier issues 200 probes with a 50-nanosecond access budget per probe and rejects any response slower than the budget. One honest agent holds 16 GB and answers in 3 ms; 10 fakes must hold 160 GB and sustain 10 parallel probe streams, costing $1,200 in RAM alone, and the sparrow log records every probe while the pigment check re-runs them under a fresh seed. A failed probe freezes the identity and slashes its bond.
